_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I: Minuchihr's vengeance on Salm and Tur; death of Faridun. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Minuchihr Slays Tur in the Night Battle
title.zh: 米努奇赫爾夜戰誅圖爾

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 19-22

summary.en: Faridun sends young Minuchihr with Karan, Garshasp, and Sam against the two murderers of Iraj. When Tur plans a night-attack, Minuchihr arranges an ambush of thirty thousand chosen warriors; Tur's host of a hundred thousand meets banners flying, and the young prince springs from ambush, surrounds him, hurles a dart into his back, and cuts off his head, sending it in a casket to Faridun: I have slain him as he slew Iraj.
summary.zh: 法里東遣米努奇赫爾率卡蘭、加爾沙斯普與薩姆征討弑伊朗支之二人。圖爾謀夜襲，米努奇赫爾預伏三萬精兵；圖爾十萬之軍夜出，見旌旗嚴陣。年輕王子自伏兵中殺出，合圍圖爾，擲鏢中背，斬其首，裝匣送呈法里東：「我以他弑伊朗支之法誅之。」

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: The Shah was told that a host had crossed Jihun, and bade prince Minuchihr to pass the frontier. The Shah was told a host had crossed, and bade prince Minuchihr pass the frontier toward the desert: a youth predestined to be fortunate may ensnare a mountain-sheep while hunters are before and pards behind; but having patience, prudence, sense, and wits, he will take savage lions in his toils.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 19 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The armies fought till night, till Minuchihr obtained the victory. Noon passed; the brothers met for consultation and said: let us attempt a night-attack and fill the desert with blood. That night those miscreants drew their army out bent on a camisade; the Iranian scouts gat news thereof and sped to Minuchihr. That shrewd man heard and planned a counter-ruse: he left Karan the host and led himself an ambuscade with thirty thousand warriors, all men of name.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 20-21 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Tur came at night and brought one hundred thousand men prepared for fight, but found the foe arrayed with banners flying and saw that battle was his sole resource. Minuchihr sprang from his ambush and surrounded Tur, who wheeled and fled mid wailings of despair from his own troops. Stay, miscreant, cried the prince, hot for revenge, who lovest fight so well and cuttest off the heads of innocents! He hurled a dart against Tur's back, whose sword fell from his grasp; then Minuchihr like wind unseated him, cast him to earth, slew him, cut off his head, and left the body for the beasts of prey.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 21 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then Minuchihr wrote to Shah Faridun: since Tur had placed within a golden casket his royal brother's head in foul contempt, and had no ruth or reverence for him, God delivered Tur to me, and I have slain him as he slew Iraj; and will lay waste his realm and dwelling-place. The messenger approached with confidence and laid the head of Tur before the Shah, who prayed to God, the righteous Judge, to pour on Minuchihr his blessings evermore.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 22 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Salm Falls by the Hand of Minuchihr

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun secs. 23-25

summary.en: Karan the avenger takes Tur's signet-ring and royal standard, gains entry to the sea-castle of the Alans as a pretended envoy, raises the standard at break of day, and Shirwi storms the gate: by noon castle and castellan had vanished, and twice six thousand of the foe were slain. Kakwi, grandson of Zahhak, then fights Minuchihr and is dragged from his steed and gashed. Salm flees to the sea, finds not a spar of vessel, and Minuchihr overtakes him and cleaves the king of Rum asunder from the neck, setting his head upon a spear.
summary.zh: 復仇者卡蘭取圖爾印信戰旗，偽作使者混入臨海阿蘭要塞，黎明高舉戰旗，希爾維奪門而入——正午時要塞與守將俱滅，敵軍一萬二千人被誅。扎哈克之孫卡克維來戰，被拖下馬砍創。薩爾姆逃至海邊，無船可渡；米努奇赫爾追及，自頸將羅姆王劈為兩半，其首懸於矛尖。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: News of the fight and of that Moon's eclipse reached Salm, who purposed making a retreat upon a lofty castle in his rear — the hold of the Alans, whose head is in the clouds, built by cunning from the ocean's depths. Karan chose six thousand veterans of name and said: I will secure Salm's only gate for combat or for retreat; for this exploit I need Tur's royal standard and his signet-ring, then will I make a shift to seize the hold.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 23 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Disguised as envoy to the castellan, Karan showed Tur's signet-ring and gave a forged charge from Tur; the castellan recognised the signet and they oped the castle-gates: he saw the seeming, but he saw no more. At break of day Karan set up a standard like the moon full-orbed and made signals to Shirwi, who seized on the gate and threw in his troops. By noon the castle's form and castellan's had vanished; at sunset hold and plain were level, and twice six thousand of the foe were slain.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 23, 25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Kakwi the grandson of Zahhak then came forth like a div, and Minuchihr advanced with Indian sword in hand; they fought till noon like pards, and as day declined the prince caught the girdle of Kakwi, dragged his elephantine form from his steed, flung him upon the burning sand, and gashed his chest with the scimitar. Kakwi being dead, Salm ceased to seek revenge and fled toward the sea, but saw not a spar of any vessel there.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun secs. 24-25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: The Iranian host pursued apace, and Minuchihr, hard upon the king of Rum, cried: thou who art guilty of the blackest crime, who murderedst thy brother for his crown, whither wilt thou flee? I bring thee now a crown and throne: the royal Tree hath come to bearing fruit. As thus he spake he urged his steed along, and in another moment overtook and clave the king asunder from the neck, then bade the head be set upon a spear.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 25 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. I, Faridun sec. 27

summary.en: Reunited with the heads of all three of his sons, Faridun lives out his days in tears and austerities: my days are changed and darkened by these three, who were my heart's delight and grief withal. Minuchihr girds a blood-stained girdle, rears a charnel of ruddy gold and lapislazuli with a throne of ivory within, hangs a crown above it, bids the dead farewell as ritual requires, and shuts the charnel-door. One sennight the whole city mourns with its mourning sovereign.
summary.zh: 三子之首皆在身側，法里東以淚與苦行度其餘年：「我的歲月被這三子改變而黯淡，他們曾是我心中的歡喜與悲傷。」米努奇赫爾繫血染腰帶，以赤金與青金石築陵，內置象牙御座，其上懸冠，依禮向死者道別而閉陵門。全城為哀慟之君服喪七日。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; no living community restriction.

passages.text: This done, the great king's day and fortune changed, the leafage withered on the royal tree; he quitted crown and throne and with the heads of those three kings beside him lived in tears and in austerities: my days are changed and darkened by these three, who were my heart's delight and grief withal, thus slain before me miserably. Such ills befell them through their perversity and evil deeds; they disobeyed me and the world frowned on them. His heart was full, his face all tears till death.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then Minuchihr put off the royal crown, he girt a blood-stained girdle round his loins, and reared a charnel as the Shahs were wont of ruddy gold and lapislazuli. They placed a throne of ivory within and hung a crown above it, visited the dead to say farewell, as was the use and ritual, then shut the charnel-door: in such ill case that dear one left the world. One sennight Minuchihr gave up to grief, and for a sennight city and bazar were mourning with their mourning sovereign.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Faridun sec. 27 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
